must_remember: Superconductivity is characterized by zero electrical DC resistance and complete diamagnetism ($B = 0$, Meissner effect) below a critical temperature $T_c$.
The transition at $T_c$ in the absence of a magnetic field is typically a thermodynamic second-order phase transition.

Type-I superconductors exhibit a complete Meissner effect up to a single critical field $H_c$, while Type-II superconductors have two critical fields ($H_{c1}$ and $H_{c2}$) with a mixed vortex state in between.
BCS theory explains superconductivity via lattice-vibration (phonon) mediated pairing of electrons into weakly bound Cooper pairs.
The magnetic flux inside a superconductor is quantized in units of $\Phi_0 = \frac{h}{2e}$.

glossary.meaning: The characteristic temperature below which a material transitions into the superconducting state.
The complete expulsion of magnetic flux from the interior of a superconductor as it transitions to the superconducting state.
The characteristic length over which a magnetic field decays inside the surface of a superconductor.
A bound pair of electrons formed through attractive phonon-mediated interaction in superconductors, acting as a composite boson.
The dependence of the critical temperature on the isotopic mass of the superconducting element, given by $T_c M^\alpha = \text{constant}$.
